bio_en: Saghatel Zohrabian came from a well-to-do family of Hamadan, where his influential father gave him the best education available. In 1893 he entered the Protestant school in Tehran, whose teachers urged his parents to send him abroad to study, but they refused, and he returned home to work at the Imperial Bank of Persia. Neither his parents' tears nor his fiancée's pleas could hold him back from avenging his martyred brethren; he left, was wounded twice in the side and leg while fighting for higher positions, and was killed. Droshak called him the first Persian-Armenian intellectual martyr for the cause.
notes: Compiled from the archive review, 2026-10-12. Confidence: medium. Years 1877-1897 from the title; the battle (probably Khanasor, 1897) is not named in the portion read.
